confirmed.title: Every Rotation change restarts the reminder cycle at quote #1, so later quotes are rarely or never shown (notifications and widget)
confirmed.evidence: RotationState.updated(with:) returns `RotationState(quoteIDs:, anchor: now, seed: new)` whenever the ID list changes (ReminderSettings.swift:157-159). ReminderStore.performReplan applies it on every replan (ReminderStore.swift:236-241). ReminderPlanner.plan sets base = ordinal(of: firstSlot, anchor) (ReminderPlanner.swift:55), which is 0 straight after a reset, so the next slot is always ids[0]. The widget's 'now' entry also falls back to ordinal 0 (ReminderPlanner.swift:117-118). New quotes default to 'Include in reminders' = true (AddEditQuoteView.swift:252), and saving a shared quote adds it to reminders (SharedInboxView.swift:58), so ordinary use changes the ID list often. Remove-with-Undo and reorders reset it too. I compiled QuotedCore with a driver in the scratchpad: 10 quotes, 3 a day, one new quote every 2 days, 30 days. Q1 to Q6 were each delivered 15 times. Q7 to Q24 were never delivered.
confirmed.scenario: A user has 10 quotes in reminders (3 a day, in order) and saves a new quote every couple of days with the default toggle on. Each save restarts the cycle at the first quote, so notifications and the widget repeat the first 6 quotes forever. The quotes at the end of the list, including every new one, never appear. This breaks F4 ('cycle through the Rotation') and F5.
confirmed.fix: Keep the cycle's progress across membership changes. In Packages/QuotedKit/Sources/QuotedCore/Reminders/ReminderSettings.swift, add `startIndex: Int` to RotationState with a custom init(from:) that uses decodeIfPresent and defaults to 0, so existing App Group and widget-snapshot JSON still decodes. Change updated(with:at:seed:) to take the old state's last delivered quote: ReminderPlanner.currentQuoteID(rotation: old, settings:, at: now), used only if at least one slot has passed since the old anchor, otherwise the quote the old state would play next. Map it to its index in the new list (or, if it was removed, its old index clamped to the new count), and set startIndex = index + 1 with anchor = now. In ReminderPlanner.swift, make QuoteMapper use (ordinal + startIndex) mod count, before the shuffle permutation. Update the call in ReminderStore.performReplan to pass settings. Add QuotedCoreTests showing that appending a quote mid-cycle continues with the next quote, and that a 10-quote rotation with periodic appends reaches every quote.
confirmed.verifierReason: Confirmed in code. RotationState.updated(with:) (ReminderSettings.swift:140-142) returns a fresh state with anchor=now whenever the ID list differs, and performReplan applies it on every replan (ReminderStore.swift:236-241). After that, plan() computes base = ordinal(of: firstSlot, anchor: now), which is 0, and currentEntry clamps to ordinal 0 (ReminderPlanner.swift:55, 117-118). So both the next notification and the widget always restart at ids[0]. The default order is .inOrder (ReminderSettings.swift:45). New quotes are appended at max+1 (LibraryStore.swift:331-333) and default to 'Include in reminders' on. Any add, remove or reorder that comes sooner than one full cycle (N / timesPerDay days) therefore restarts the cycle, and the tail of the list, which includes every newly added quote, is never shown. The docs make the restart deliberate (system-design.md:129, app-architecture.md:244), but the result breaks F4 ('cycle through the Rotation') for any user who adds quotes more often than once per cycle. That is a realistic path for a core feature, so high stands. Shuffle is less affected because each restart draws a fresh random permutation.

confirmed.title: Library, inbox and friendships fetches have no pagination and are silently cut at PostgREST max_rows=1000; Rotation writes are O(N) and put every ID in the URL
confirmed.evidence: fetchMine (QuotesRepository.swift:10-21), inbox() (SocialRepository.swift:262-272) and friendships() (SocialRepository.swift:92-103) have no range or limit. supabase/config.toml:18 sets max_rows = 1000, which is also the hosted default. LibraryStore.refresh replaces the whole local copy with the result (LibraryStore.swift:106), and search, reminders and the cache read only that copy. setRotation selects `id in (<every rotation id>)` and then upserts every rotation row, body included (QuotesRepository.swift:81-93). LibraryStore.addToReminders/removeFromReminders send the full current list (LibraryStore.swift:219-232). nextReminderPosition uses the local maximum (LibraryStore.swift:331-333). The design promises 'at most a few thousand rows' (docs/system-design.md:112) and 'Revisit past about 5k quotes' (docs/system-design.md:167).
confirmed.scenario: A user with 1,200 quotes gets only the newest 1,000. The oldest 200 drop out of the Library, Search and the cache with no error. Any of them in reminders stop appearing in notifications and the widget. The next add or reorder renumbers only the visible reminder quotes from 0, so the hidden ones keep their old positions and collide. Each single toggle also re-sends every reminder ID in the GET URL and re-uploads every body. With a few hundred reminder quotes, that means a very long query string and up to ~1 MB of upload per tap. Received shares cannot be deleted, so the inbox keeps growing and hits the same cap.
confirmed.fix: Packages/QuotedKit/Sources/QuotedKit/Services/QuotesRepository.swift: replace the select+upsert in setRotation with a SECURITY INVOKER RPC in a new migration, e.g. public.set_rotation(ordered uuid[], removed uuid[]). It runs one UPDATE ... FROM unnest(ordered) WITH ORDINALITY on the caller's own rows, nulls `removed`, and returns the updated rows. The arrays travel in the POST body, so there is no URL growth, no bodies and no prior select. Grant execute to authenticated and add pgTAP tests. Also compute the next position server-side. In fetchMine, inbox() and friendships(), page with .range(from:to:) in a loop until a short page comes back (or keyset on created_at,id), so results are never cut at max_rows.
confirmed.verifierReason: Confirmed. fetchMine, inbox() and friendships() have no range or paging (QuotesRepository.swift:10-21, SocialRepository.swift:92-103, 262-272), and max_rows = 1000 (config.toml:18; hosted default is the same). refresh() replaces the local copy wholesale (LibraryStore.swift:106), so the oldest rows above 1000 disappear silently. Users that large are rare at MVP, but the design promises 'at most a few thousand rows'. The Rotation-write part bites much sooner, and I reproduced it. setRotation sends every reminder ID in a GET `id=in.(...)` filter, and the SDK encodes commas as %2C (39 chars per UUID). Against the LOCAL stack, a request line of about 8 KB returned 401 (it passed the gateway), while 8.2 KB and above returned HTTP 414 URI Too Long. That threshold is about 205 IDs. So a user with roughly 205 or more quotes in reminders (new quotes and starters default to included) cannot add, remove or reorder any reminder: each attempt applies optimistically, then fails with an error toast and reverts (LibraryStore.swift:219-232, 347-370). The hosted gateway's limit is unverified but likely similar. Medium fits.

confirmed.title: Pending deletes and shares are committed on background without a background-task assertion, so suspension can drop them silently
confirmed.evidence: sceneDidEnterBackground awaits toasts.flushPending(), which runs the deferred commit: backend.quotes.delete, or backend.social.share for a share (AppModel.swift:142-148, Toast.swift flushPending). The code has no UIApplication.beginBackgroundTask or performExpiringActivity anywhere (grep finds none). The docs say the commit runs 'when the app backgrounds' (docs/app-architecture.md:287). Only a kill inside the 5 s window is an accepted loss (app-architecture.md:403). POST and DELETE get no SDK retry.
confirmed.scenario: A user taps Send to Maya, sees 'Sent to Maya' and goes to the Home Screen within 5 s. The flush starts the POST, then iOS suspends the app a moment later on a slow cellular link, before the token refresh and insert finish. If iOS later reclaims the app, the share is never sent and nobody is told. If the app survives, the request fails on resume and a 'Couldn't send' toast shows up out of context. The same applies to a quote delete: the quote comes back on the next refresh.
confirmed.fix: App/AppModel.swift sceneDidEnterBackground (and ideally ToastCenter.flushPending in App/Design/Components/Toast.swift): take `let id = UIApplication.shared.beginBackgroundTask(withName: "FlushPending") { ... }` before `await toasts.flushPending()` and call endBackgroundTask(id) after it, including from the expiration handler. For shares, also persist the pending send (recipient IDs, quote snapshot, note) to the App Group before the commit and retry it on next launch if it never confirmed.
confirmed.verifierReason: Confirmed. RootView fires `Task { await app.sceneDidEnterBackground() }` on .background (RootView.swift:37-42), which awaits toasts.flushPending(), and that runs the deferred commit (quote delete or share POST). Nothing in App, Widgets or QuotedKit calls beginBackgroundTask or performExpiringActivity. iOS suspends an app shortly after it backgrounds unless it holds an assertion. On a slow link, or when a token refresh is needed first, the request can be cut off: it is lost if the app is later jettisoned, or fails out of context on resume. Normal networks finish within the grace period, so this is an edge case. The share half also depends on the known 'Undo by delaying the send 5s' design and goes away if that changes. The delete half only resurrects the quote. Medium is the upper bound.

confirmed.title: URLSession.shared's disk cache keeps auth tokens and library/inbox responses, and nothing clears it on sign-out or account deletion
confirmed.evidence: Backend.init defaults `urlSession: URLSession = .shared` (Backend.swift:50) and passes it to the SDK as `global: .init(headers: headers, session: urlSession)` (:65). Auth, PostgREST and Functions all go through it. Nothing in App/ or QuotedKit uses URLCache, `.ephemeral`, `requestCachePolicy` or `removeAllCachedResponses`. SessionStore.endSession (App/Stores/SessionStore.swift:369-391) wipes only the App Group, prefs and notifications. I copied the simulator's Library/Caches/com.hwei.quoted/Cache.db and inspected the copy. It holds entry 1 `POST /auth/v1/signup`, whose 2,112-byte body contains `access_token`, `refresh_token` and `email`. It also holds GET responses for /rest/v1/quotes (the full library select), /rest/v1/shares (the inbox with body/note), /rest/v1/friendships with embedded profiles, and /rest/v1/starter_quotes (stored in fsCachedData). The bundled privacy.md:44 says "Signing out removes the cached library, widget data and scheduled reminders from your device."
confirmed.scenario: A user signs in (the /token password or PKCE response is cached the same way the signup response was), then signs out or deletes their account. Cache.db and fsCachedData under Library/Caches still hold a session token pair, their email, their whole quote library, their inbox (friends' shared quotes and notes) and their friend list. Anyone with file access to the container (forensic extraction, a jailbroken or shared device, a sysdiagnose-style dump) can read them, and the tokens sit outside the Keychain. Keep the injection point for tests. In App/Stores/SessionStore.swift endSession and once at launch, call `URLCache.shared.removeAllCachedResponses()` to purge caches written by earlier builds and TestFlight installs.

confirmed.title: body_format on quotes and shares has no byte limit: a 20 MB row is accepted, so any user can fill the database and a friend can bloat every inbox fetch
confirmed.evidence: The only checks are `jsonb_typeof(body_format) = 'array' and jsonb_array_length(body_format) <= 200` (core_schema.sql:52-54 for quotes, :129-131 for shares). The element shape and size are not checked, and there is no per-user quota. I ran a probe as `authenticated` in a rolled-back transaction on the local stack. `insert into quotes (body, body_format) select 'x', jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('junk', repeat(md5(g::text),3200)))` over 200 rows was accepted (pg_column_size 20 MB). A quote deleted the same way comes back on the next launch: the cache was never rewritten and the server row still exists. (b) The user sends, then presses Home. confirmed.title: refresh() overwrites local state with a snapshot fetched before concurrent creates/deletes committed (quotes vanish or resurrect)
confirmed.evidence: LibraryStore.refresh assigns `quotes = Self.sorted(fetched.filter { !pendingDeletes.contains($0.id) })` (line 106) with no generation or in-flight-mutation check, then writes the cache and replans (lines 110-111). Concurrent mutations update `quotes` directly: create→upsertLocal (line 140), saveShared (line 280), and commitDelete removes the ID from pendingDeletes as soon as the server answers (line 196). Refreshes are not de-duplicated, so enterReady, foreground, tab and pull-to-refresh can overlap, and an older response can land last. SocialStore.refresh (SocialStore.swift:126-127) likewise replaces `inbox` and the friend arrays wholesale over markSavedLocally and markSeen.
confirmed.scenario: At cold launch, enterReady starts refreshIfStale(maxAge: 30) on a slow cellular link. The user taps +, pastes a quote and saves. create() returns first and the quote appears, then the stale fetch lands and replaces the list without it. The cache and widget are rewritten without it, and lastRefreshed was just set, so it stays hidden until a pull-to-refresh or 60 s later. The user assumes the save failed and adds it again, creating a duplicate. Conversely, a fetch that read the DB just before a delete commit but returns after it puts the deleted quote back in the list and cache. Editing that ghost quote later fails with "We couldn't find that." In the inbox, a share just saved flips back from "Saved" to "Save".
confirmed.fix: Add a `mutationGeneration` counter to LibraryStore, bumped in upsertLocal, commitDelete and the writeRotation success path. Capture it before `fetchMine()` and, if it changed by the time the response arrives, either discard the result (and leave lastRefreshed unset so the next trigger refetches) or merge: re-apply locally created quotes missing from `fetched` and keep recently deleted IDs (a `recentlyDeleted` set cleared only by a refresh that started after the commit) filtered out. Coalesce refresh() into a single in-flight `Task` that later callers await. Do the same in SocialStore.refresh for savedAt and seenAt.
confirmed.verifierReason: Confirmed. LibraryStore.refresh assigns `quotes = Self.sorted(fetched.filter { !pendingDeletes.contains($0.id) })` (line 106) with no check for mutations that finished while the fetch was in flight. It then sets lastRefreshed, writes the cache and replans (108-111). create → upsertLocal (140) and saveShared (280) change `quotes` directly. commitDelete drops the ID from pendingDeletes as soon as the server answers (196). Refreshes are not coalesced: enterReady starts refreshIfStale(maxAge: 30) (SessionStore.swift:352), and sceneDidBecomeActive, tab appear and pull-to-refresh start more. So a fetch whose database read came before a create or delete commit, and whose response lands after it, overwrites the local result. The saved quote disappears from the list, cache and widget until the next refresh (lastRefreshed was just set, so up to 60 s and a foreground), or a deleted quote comes back and editing it later fails. SocialStore.refresh (126-127) has the same overwrite for markSavedLocally and markSeen. It is a race that needs a slow fetch (a large library on a poor link at cold launch), so medium is the right level.

confirmed.title: Undo toasts expire after a fixed 5 s and VoiceOver users can't reach Undo in time

When the timer ends, `dismiss()` commits the deferred delete or send.
confirmed.scenario: A VoiceOver user deletes a quote with the row's Delete custom action, removes a quote from reminders, or blocks someone. They hear "Quote deleted", then have to swipe through every element on screen to reach the toast pinned above the tab bar. That takes longer than 5 s, so the delete commits and Undo is effectively unavailable to them (WCAG 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable). Switch Control users hit the same limit.
confirmed.fix: In Toast.swift, when `UIAccessibility.isVoiceOverRunning || UIAccessibility.isSwitchControlRunning`, use a longer duration (for example 15 s), or don't auto-expire an actionable toast. confirmed.title: Offline, writes that start with a GET wait ~7 s of SDK retries before failing; failed reminder toggles revert late and stall the write queue

The onboarding flag lives in App Group defaults, so it is missing on a new device and after a reinstall, where the Keychain session survives and sign-in is automatic.

Go to .needsStarter only when the refresh succeeded and returned no quotes.

confirmed.title: Refresh results have no ordering guard, so a slow refresh can overwrite newer optimistic writes; rotation success does not replan
confirmed.evidence: LibraryStore.refresh only checks that the user is unchanged before `quotes = ...fetched` and replan (LibraryStore.swift:98-112). Nothing tracks in-flight creates, updates or rotation writes; only pendingDeletes is protected. SocialStore.refresh likewise replaces friends and inbox wholesale (SocialStore.swift:116-131) even if accept or block changed them meanwhile. writeRotation's success path upserts the server rows but never calls reminders.replan() (LibraryStore.swift:357-360). Refreshes run concurrently from foreground, pull-to-refresh, enterReady and the tab .task modifiers, with no single-flight guard.
confirmed.scenario: On a slow network, foregrounding starts a library fetch, and the user adds a quote to reminders or saves a new quote before the large response arrives. The response, reflecting the server before the write, lands last. The new quote disappears, or the reminder toggle reverts, until the next refresh 60 s or more later. If the stale refresh lands between the optimistic apply and the server's confirmation, the final list is correct, but notifications and the widget keep the stale order until the next foreground. In Friends, an accepted request can reappear as incoming, and tapping Accept again gives 'We couldn't find that'.
confirmed.fix: App/Stores/LibraryStore.swift: add `private var mutationGeneration = 0`, incremented in create, update, delete, writeRotation, importStarter and saveShared. In refresh, capture it before fetchMine and drop the result (or retry once) if it changed. Make refresh single-flight by reusing an in-flight Task. Call reminders.replan() after a successful setRotation upsert. Apply the same generation guard in App/Stores/SocialStore.swift around accept, decline, cancel, removeFriend and block.
confirmed.verifierReason: Confirmed. LibraryStore.refresh only guards against a user change before overwriting `quotes` with the fetched list (LibraryStore.swift:98-112). It has no generation counter or single flight, and does not track in-flight creates, updates or rotation writes (only pendingDeletes). SocialStore.refresh likewise overwrites friends and inbox (SocialStore.swift:116-131), while accept() mutates them optimistically (190-204). writeRotation's success path upserts the rows but does not replan, so a stale refresh that replanned in between leaves notifications and the widget on the old order. These are real races, but they need a slow refresh that overlaps a user write, and the next refresh heals them. Low.

confirmed.title: Retrying account deletion after the first call succeeded server-side shows 'session ended' and skips the local wipe

confirmed.title: Anyone can file a report about any user with made-up content, and once a block nulls share_id it looks the same as a server-verified report
confirmed.evidence: The 'reports: file as yourself' policy (core_schema.sql:445-459) accepts `share_id is null` for any `reported_user_id`, with no relationship required and no rate limit. Report_snapshot.sql:9-13 keeps the client's content_body/author/source when share_id is null, and the trigger copies server content only when share_id is set (:44-50). A block deletes the shares, so `reports.share_id ... on delete set null` (core_schema.sql:157) turns a verified report into share_id=null too. No column records which kind it was. A local rolled-back probe confirmed: as A, `insert into reports (reported_user_id, reason, content_body, created_at) values (<stranger C>, 'harassment', 'fabricated text', '2000-01-01')` succeeds. Also, `reported_user_id ... on delete cascade` (:158) erases every report about a user when that user deletes their account.
confirmed.scenario: An attacker lists profiles (all are readable) and files backdated 'harassment' reports against a target, with abusive text they made up. The developer reviews them in the dashboard, sees content_body on rows with share_id null (the same shape as genuine report-then-block cases), and bans or deletes an innocent account. In the other direction, a real abuser deletes their account and every report against them disappears, so a repeat offender cannot be recognised.
confirmed.fix: Add `snapshot_verified boolean not null default false` to reports. Set it to true in private.reports_snapshot_share when the share row was found, and force it to false otherwise, so the client cannot set it. Show the column in dashboard review. Optionally force created_at := now() in the same trigger (see the timestamps finding).
confirmed.verifierReason: The mechanics are accurate. The reports insert policy (core_schema.sql:445-459) allows share_id null for any reported_user_id with no relationship check. The trigger copies server content only when share_id is set (report_snapshot.sql:44-50). A block nulls share_id through the FK, and no column records whether the snapshot was server-copied. Much of this is documented design, though. report_snapshot.sql:11-13 and system-design.md:81/90 say share_id-null snapshots are 'the reporter's account', and system-design.md:70 documents that social tables cascade through profiles, so reports vanishing on account deletion is intended data deletion. The real gap is narrow: after report-then-block, a reviewer cannot tell a server-verified snapshot from client-supplied text. That class is not ThisDeviceOnly, and iOS keeps Keychain items after an app is uninstalled. `emitLocalSessionAsInitialSession: true` (:63) restores the stored session at launch. There is no first-launch Keychain wipe in Release; UITestReset is DEBUG only (QuotedApp.swift:86-112).

confirmed.title: Optimistic rollbacks restore whole-state snapshots, clobbering concurrent mutations (reminders and friend requests end in states the server never had)
confirmed.evidence: writeRotation captures `before` (line 348) after any earlier queued write's optimistic change has already been applied. On failure (lines 362-366) it restores every quote's position from that snapshot. SocialStore uses the same pattern with tuples of whole arrays: accept (SocialStore.swift:192 snapshot, :200 restore), block (:230/:245) and removeConnection (:400/:408). Each restores arrays that may already contain other in-flight operations' optimistic edits, or lack them.
confirmed.scenario: Offline, the user taps "Add to reminders" on quote A, then on quote B. W1 (A) fails, rolls back to the state before A and awaits refresh(), which also fails offline. W2 (B) then fails and restores its snapshot, which still contains A at the end of the reminders. Both showed error toasts, yet A is now shown in reminders, and replan() schedules notifications and the widget for A, although the server never stored it. A later refresh removes it silently. In SocialStore, accepting two incoming requests offline makes r1's failure restore S0 and then r2's failure restore S1, so r1 is shown as a friend while the server still has it pending. Sharing to that person then fails with "You can only share with friends." Online, a failed accept of r1 restores r2 to incoming after r2's decline already succeeded.
confirmed.fix: Roll back only what the failed operation changed. LibraryStore.writeRotation: on failure, skip the snapshot restore and rely on the existing `await refresh()` (or restore only the IDs in `ordered`/`removing` whose current position still equals what this write applied). confirmed.title: The sign-out wipe of the App Group can be undone by an in-flight detached library-cache write
confirmed.evidence: writeCache() starts a detached utility-priority Task chain (lines 299-307) and nothing awaits it. SessionStore.signOut calls `await toasts.flushPending()` (SessionStore.swift:234). A pending delete commit ends with writeCache() (LibraryStore.swift:197). Then signOut removes the session, and the session listener or signOut runs endSession, which calls `appGroup?.wipeAll()` (SessionStore.swift:389) without awaiting `library.cacheWrite`.
confirmed.scenario: The user deletes a quote and taps Sign Out within the Undo window. The flush commits the delete and queues a cache write that encodes the whole library and inbox at utility QoS. The main actor reaches wipeAll() a few milliseconds later, and the write lands after the wipe. library-cache.json, holding the signed-out user's quotes and received shares, stays in the shared container after sign-out until someone signs in again. That contradicts the documented "signing out wipes the App Group".
confirmed.fix: Add `func waitForCacheWrites() async { await cacheWrite?.value }` to LibraryStore. In SessionStore.endSession, call it after library.reset() and before appGroup?.wipeAll(). confirmed.verifierReason: There is no ordering between the detached cache write and the wipe. writeCache() starts a Task.detached(priority: .utility) chain that nothing awaits (LibraryStore.swift:296-308). signOut flushes pending toasts (a delete commit ends with writeCache(), line 197), signs out with scope .local (no network round trip, AuthService.swift:56), and endSession calls appGroup?.wipeAll() (SessionStore.swift:389) without awaiting library.cacheWrite. The only delay is `await reminders.cancelAll()` (a few UNUserNotificationCenter IPC calls), so a utility-QoS encode and atomic write can occasionally land after the wipe. Only LibraryStore.prepare reads it, through readLibraryCache(for:), which requires a matching userID (AppGroupStore.swift:96-99), and the next user's first writeCache overwrites it. rejected.title: Debug builds run against the production project and log web_search_tap events into the metric that decides the roadmap
rejected.reason: The facts are right. The Quoted scheme runs Debug (project.yml:106-107), Debug.xcconfig includes Hosted.xcconfig, and logWebSearchTap is gated only by sideEffects. But this is a documented configuration choice (system-design.md:142 'Debug: hosted Supabase (default Run)'), and it has no effect on users or the shipped app. Every event row carries user_id (core_schema.sql:187), so the developer's own test accounts can be excluded from the web_search_tap decision query. That makes the claimed harm (a skewed build-or-not decision) speculative and easily avoided. It is analytics hygiene, not a defect.

rejected.title: Every profile is readable in bulk, and friend requests can be sent and re-sent without limit, even straight after a decline
rejected.reason: The behaviour is by design and disclosed. system-design.md:76 states profiles are 'select: any authenticated user, since usernames are public handles', and privacy.md:35 tells users 'Your username and display name are visible to other signed-in Quoted users.' Re-requesting after a decline (a DELETE) is standard social-app behaviour. The user can block from the request row's context menu (FriendsView.swift:161), and is_blocked_pair then stops further requests, which meets the 1.2 block requirement. GoTrue sign-up rate limits make new accounts slower. Per-requester rate limits and directory hiding would harden the app, but nothing here is broken.

rejected.title: The server's auth policy is weaker than the client's: 6-character passwords, and a config with confirmations off that allows email enumeration
rejected.reason: The impact does not hold up. The server's 6-character minimum only lets someone who bypasses the UI give their own account a weaker password, which harms only that person. Hosted auth settings are set in the dashboard, not by config.toml. The email-enumeration path needs 'Confirm email' off in production, but deploy-backend.sh:84-85 says it is optional for MVP testing only and to turn it back on before release. The app already handles the confirmation flow (SessionStore.pendingConfirmationEmail, AuthFlowView 'Check your inbox'), so nothing forces it off. secure_password_change matters only with the set-new-password screen, which is a known gap. These are hardening suggestions, not a defect.

rejected.title: The Release (App Store) Info.plist ships an ATS exception, NSAllowsLocalNetworking, that only the Debug-Local stack needs
rejected.reason: The fact is true: App/Info.plist:46-50 ships NSAllowsLocalNetworking in every configuration. But there is no concrete failure. The app connects only to the compile-time SUPABASE_URL (https hosted in Release), so the exception opens no reachable cleartext path. Apple's ATS documentation says NSAllowsLocalNetworking needs no App Review justification, unlike NSAllowsArbitraryLoads, so the claim that Review may ask about it does not hold. This is hygiene, not a defect.

rejected.title: The current archive is unsigned and has no Team, and the documented rename step for a taken bundle ID omits the hard-coded App Group constant in Swift
